answer: A work-backed staking bond resists sybil attacks: each agent identity must lock a refundable deposit earned through verified work, never bought in bulk. A sparrow-light newcomer starts with tiny limits, while a hollow shell account with no history cannot borrow reputation. A marble-solid audit trail ties every deposit to completed tasks, so forging a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds. The attacker pays linearly while defenders verify cheaply, making mass forgery unprofitable.
